options.metric: Number of crash rows grouped by weekday of crash_date
options.denominator: No denominator; raw count of crash rows
options.grouping: Weekday of crash_date, Monday through Sunday
options.chart_type: Vertical bar chart of crash-row counts
options.reason: A raw count is a direct way to show the total recorded crash volume assigned to each weekday over the requested period.
options.answer: Across 2,132,218 police-reported crash rows dated 2013–2025, Friday has the most (338,800) and Sunday the fewest (257,544).
options.interpretation: Each bar counts one police-reported NYC motor-vehicle-crash row with crash_date in 2013–2025, grouped Monday–Sunday, and there is no denominator; Friday has 338,800 rows (most) and Sunday 257,544 (fewest). This raw-total framing answers the overall recorded-crash volume by weekday, but not exposure-adjusted rates, people involved, or year-specific changes. Included annual row counts were 203,742 (2013), 206,046 (2014), 217,708 (2015), 229,833 (2016), 231,007 (2017), 231,564 (2018), 211,486 (2019), 112,918 (2020), 110,558 (2021), 103,887 (2022), 96,607 (2023), 91,316 (2024), and 85,546 (2025); the shift after 2018 means pooled raw weekday totals combine very different yearly volumes and cannot describe within-year weekday patterns. Checks found 136,969 dated rows outside the period excluded, no missing crash dates, no impossible or conventional-default dates among included records, and observed January 1–December 31 dates in every year; all in-period rows were kept, though boundary observations do not prove complete reporting.

options.metric: Percentage of all in-period crash rows attributed to each weekday of crash_date
options.denominator: All 2,132,218 included crash rows with crash_date in 2013–2025
options.grouping: Weekday of crash_date, Monday through Sunday
options.chart_type: Vertical bar chart of shares of all in-period crash rows
options.reason: A share expresses the weekday mix on a common 100% scale and is easy to interpret as the composition of all recorded crashes.
options.answer: Friday accounts for the largest share of in-period police-reported crashes (15.89%), while Sunday accounts for the smallest (12.08%).
options.interpretation: Each bar is the weekday's crash-row count divided by all 2,132,218 police-reported NYC crash rows with crash_date in 2013–2025, with weekdays Monday–Sunday; Friday is 15.89% and Sunday 12.08%. This answers the composition of the pooled record set, a defensible distribution measure that puts weekdays on a common percentage scale, but it does not show exposure-adjusted risk or annual changes in weekday mix. Included annual row counts were 203,742 (2013), 206,046 (2014), 217,708 (2015), 229,833 (2016), 231,007 (2017), 231,564 (2018), 211,486 (2019), 112,918 (2020), 110,558 (2021), 103,887 (2022), 96,607 (2023), 91,316 (2024), and 85,546 (2025); therefore the pooled shares weight years by their number of recorded crashes and should not be read as year-by-year shares. Checks found 136,969 dated rows outside the period excluded, no missing crash dates, no impossible or conventional-default dates among included records, and observed January 1–December 31 dates in every year; all in-period rows were kept, though boundary observations do not prove complete reporting.

options.metric: Mean number of crash rows per calendar occurrence of each weekday over 2013–2025
options.denominator: Number of calendar dates of that weekday from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (678 or 679 dates, depending on weekday)
options.grouping: Weekday of crash_date, Monday through Sunday
options.chart_type: Vertical bar chart of mean crash rows per calendar weekday
options.reason: Dividing by the number of dates each weekday occurs removes the small difference in weekday opportunities across the 2013–2025 calendar period.
options.answer: Averaged over its 678 calendar dates, Friday had 499.71 police-reported crash rows per day, compared with 379.86 per Sunday date.
options.interpretation: For each weekday Monday–Sunday, this metric is its police-reported NYC crash-row total dated 2013–2025 divided by the number of calendar dates of that weekday in 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (678 for Monday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday; 679 for Tuesday and Wednesday); Friday averages 499.71 rows per date and Sunday 379.86. This is a defensible typical-calendar-day framing that adjusts for the slight difference in weekday occurrences, but it does not adjust for traffic exposure or report annual-specific averages. Included annual row counts were 203,742 (2013), 206,046 (2014), 217,708 (2015), 229,833 (2016), 231,007 (2017), 231,564 (2018), 211,486 (2019), 112,918 (2020), 110,558 (2021), 103,887 (2022), 96,607 (2023), 91,316 (2024), and 85,546 (2025); because each calendar date is equally represented, years with more crash rows still contribute higher daily counts, and these pooled averages do not establish within-year changes. Checks found 136,969 dated rows outside the period excluded, no missing crash dates, no impossible or conventional-default dates among included records, and observed January 1–December 31 dates in every year; all in-period rows were kept, though boundary observations do not prove complete reporting.
